reviews.review: Good game - worth it for the campaign. Arguably the best way to experience the Warhammer 40K universe that's not a tactical strategy game. I'd wait for a sale for a game this old, but it stands up if you love the feel of being a stompy smurf marine. The multiplayer was fun back in the day, but I'm not sure if there's a community for it now.

The game is everything the title said, is all about space marine. 
Best part in the game: You get to use most of the weapon in the Warhammer 40K nova, not all but most. You get to fight like Astartes, also know as space marine. Like cutting, tearing and skydrop using jetpack. 
Now the bad pact in the game: You can heal only using skill which can only fully charge when you hit enemy, by then I don't know how to use the skill because I forgot about which button. By the time I know is like after I have clear 25% of the map. The boss fight feel like rush, is end too fast and the last boss is disappointing, you need 4 button to bet the boss and the end story...
The story is good, there have cool pact. The whole time, you will just happy you get to play as space marine and that that. Thank you for reading c(l.lc)
It really makes you feel like the man child that you are.

Never got the chance to play. Heard a lot of good things about it and wanted to give it a go before Two came out, but can't get it to run on my current setup. I'm running Ubuntu 22.04, and in all honesty I didn't really know what to expect with a new OS, but this isn't the only title I've had trouble getting to run, and I'm starting to have my concerns with making future purchases unless I can get it figured out.

I tried reinstalling, I tried "gamemoderun PROTON_USE_WINED3D11=1 %command%" in the "Launch Options", there was something someone had said about replacing the ".EXE" but never could make heads or tails of it, and something about moving the files and appmanifest_xxxxx.acf from the wine prefix the linux steam library which was the closest I got to getting it to work, but it got to the final popup before launch and said it was missing the ".EXE".

So I would tell you unless you're absolutly sure it'll run on your OS to not purchase, or you got the experience to make it launch might not be worth the effort.
Probably the best 40K games on the market 11/10  cant wait for the 2nd addition of captain's adventures in the 2nd space marine game
